hits.heading: D11. Cote 44, scan 8, proposed general intermediate Jacobians
hits.snippet: Ottem and Suzuki (2020, Corollaries 1.2 and 4.2) construct a complex fourfold for which the Abel–Jacobi map on algebraically trivial codimension-three cycles is not the universal regular homomorphism.

hits.heading: D11. Cote 44, scan 8, proposed general intermediate Jacobians

hits.heading: D12. Cote 44, scan 4, Theorem 5 and fibration margin
hits.snippet: Künnemann (2001, Theorem 1.6) constructs height pairings for homologically trivial cycles on abelian varieties over number fields, extending the divisor–zero-cycle Néron–Tate pairing; the construction uses regular models and extensions orthogonal to cycles in special fibres.

hits.heading: Research notes
hits.snippet: These notes are separate from the diplomatic transcription. A quoted reading retains its uncertainty; mathematical comments do not authorise changes to the text. No claim of novelty is made.

hits.heading: 16:3:1 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: The claim is that a subring containing every graded projector inherits the homogeneous decomposition of the endomorphism ring. A proof has to use the finiteness of the grading to ensure that the displayed sums remain algebraic sums inside the subring, and then check multiplication of the components.

hits.heading: 16:3:2 — conjecture
hits.snippet: The page explicitly opens the converse problem of reconstructing a grading from elements labelled π_i. The opening is continued on the next scan; the conditions must be read there before deciding whether the question is answered.

hits.heading: 16:4:1 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: Orthogonal idempotents summing to one are asserted to induce the required homogeneous decomposition. The subsequent block decomposition supplies a proof strategy; the marginal extension from ℤ to an arbitrary group would require careful attention to the order of multiplication for a noncommutative grading group.

hits.heading: 16:4:4 — conjecture
hits.snippet: **Location:** cote 16, scan 4, paragraph 3, continues next scan.

hits.heading: 16:5:2 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: The commutant description identifies the projectors as central idempotents of the degree-zero subring. A direct verification must keep distinct centrality in E^0 and centrality in the whole graded ring; the latter is not asserted here.

hits.heading: 16:5:3 — reading question
hits.snippet: The written base-case insertion appears to say that all projectors except π_n are known when i=n−1; this does not immediately match the neighbouring interval statement. The indices should be rechecked against the next page and the ink, with any mathematical repair confined to the notes.

hits.heading: 16:5:4 — unpursued implication
hits.snippet: The extremal homogeneous piece can be isolated by the two complementary tail idempotents, leaving just one matrix block. This gives a route to reconstructing the next pair of projectors from annihilators or support ideals; the next sheet should determine which extra condition is used.

hits.heading: 16:6:1 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: This is the key uniqueness step: in a commutative ring an idempotent is determined by its annihilator, since its complementary principal ideal records the same decomposition. The argument also requires that the relevant projectors lie in the centre of E^0, as established on the preceding sheet.

hits.heading: 16:6:2 — unpursued implication
hits.snippet: The conditions are offered as an inductive recovery procedure, not merely as an abstract uniqueness test. A practical formulation would specify how the annihilator ideals are obtained from the known outer projectors and when those ideals are generated by idempotents.

hits.heading: 16:6:3 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: Joint injectivity of the block maps and generation of the target by their images are proposed as sufficient conditions for the two annihilator implications. Both implications can be checked on elements of the graded module; their converses would require additional hypotheses and are not stated here.

hits.heading: 16:6:4 — unpursued implication
hits.snippet: A single invertible map in the relevant homogeneous block implies both joint kernel and image conditions. This is the immediate route from a Lefschetz-type isomorphism to uniqueness of the grading projectors; the continuation must be read before assigning its full scope.

hits.heading: 16:7:1 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: The module argument is recast internally in the graded ring using two homogeneous elements that are mutual inverses on the specified projector blocks. The displayed calculation proves the first annihilator implication and refers to the second by symmetry; one should check that the degree-zero element commutes with the projectors in precisely the manner alrea

hits.heading: 16:7:2 — own idea
hits.snippet: The paired relations can be read as an equivalence between the idempotents π_i and π_{2n−i} implemented by opposite homogeneous matrix blocks. A useful test is to formulate the uniqueness mechanism in the idempotent completion of the one-object ring category, distinguishing equivalence of the corresponding summands from equality of the chosen projectors.

hits.heading: 16:7:2 — own idea
hits.snippet: **Editorial confidence:** medium. The relations are the concrete inverse identities in the relevant corners, but the manuscript has not yet supplied a categorical formulation.

hits.heading: 16:8:1 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: The sheet gives a descent argument for projectors initially defined in a larger graded ring F. The two restricted operators v′_i and w′_i lie in E, and their products recover the extremal projectors; the induction requires the previous tail-projector construction and finite support.

hits.heading: 16:8:2 — reading question
hits.snippet: The induction is rewritten several times and again has a potentially delicate terminal index. Compare this formulation with the corresponding insertion on scan5 before deciding whether the text has an indexing slip or a different convention for what is already known.

hits.heading: 16:8:3 — own idea
hits.snippet: A computational version of the proof could generate the smallest graded subring containing the homogeneous inverse pairs and recursively extract every π_i as a word in those elements. This would distinguish an existence theorem for projectors from a constructive bound on the expressions needed to produce them.

hits.heading: 16:8:3 — own idea
hits.snippet: **Editorial confidence:** medium. The displayed products explicitly recover two projectors at a time, but effective bounds and uniqueness of the resulting words are not developed on this page.

hits.heading: 16:9:1 — unpursued implication
hits.snippet: The Lefschetz-type isomorphisms are used to infer uniqueness of the grading projectors before the existence of their inverses inside the chosen subring is assumed. The distinction between uniqueness under (6.1) and descent/existence under the strengthened (6.2) should be kept explicit.

hits.heading: 16:9:2 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: The pair of module conditions is recast as ring identities involving L and homogeneous inverses w_i. The equivalence requires restriction to the indicated graded summands and extension of the inverse by the projectors; the manuscript makes the availability of those projectors part of the intrinsic formulation.

hits.heading: 16:9:4 — own idea
hits.snippet: The primitive-component projectors π_{i,α} offer a sharper test than the coarse degree projectors: one can ask which lie in the subring generated by L and the permitted inverse operators. The ensuing formulae should determine whether the manuscript proves this stronger membership statement or only introduces the notation.

hits.heading: 16:9:4 — own idea
hits.snippet: **Editorial confidence:** medium. The notation is explicit, but the construction of these finer projectors has not yet appeared on this sheet.

hits.heading: 16:10:1 — reading question

hits.heading: 16:10:2 — unproved claim
hits.snippet: The theorem connects existence of homogeneous inverses, membership of the grading projectors and membership of Λ in the subring. The item numbering and the hypotheses have been revised, and the proof continues; a clean reconstruction must state exactly which version of each hypothesis is being analysed.

hits.heading: 16:10:3 — unpursued implication
hits.snippet: The claimed membership extends from the coarse grading projectors to all primitive-component projectors. This is stronger than the existence statement on scan8 and would make the primitive decomposition intrinsic to the indicated graded ring together with the operator.
